data.hypothesis: The measured parent uses four row accumulators per thread in a 32x32 output tile; it was correct and measured at 0.0147256 s, while the one-output-per-thread baseline measured 0.273484 s. This candidate keeps four FP32 accumulators per thread, 256 threads and 1024 outputs per CTA, but changes to one row and four column stripes per thread in an 8x128 tile. Each warp then accesses contiguous B and C stripes and reuses an A value across four outputs. This tests the opposite operand-reuse/layout mapping; its register, occupancy, correctness and timing effects remain to be measured.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use the measured four-row parent as a contrasting mapping reference; the new column-stripe layout changes reuse direction while retaining four accumulators per thread and the same output count per CTA.
memory_lessons.claim: The four-row register-blocked parent was correct with a measured mean of 0.0147256 s; the measured one-output-per-thread baseline mean was 0.273484 s. These observations motivate a contrasting mapping, but do not establish that register reuse alone caused the difference or provide register/occupancy measurements.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this one-row/four-column-stripe mapping against the one-output baseline and four-row parent on the same correctness cases and repeated-timing protocol; collect register and occupancy diagnostics if available.

data.notes: This candidate is unmeasured. The supplied parent and baseline each have repeated timing observations, but no register-count or occupancy results are available. The kernel uses scalar FP32 operations and guards the column and row tails; alpha and beta are applied once per valid output.
transformations: Changed the register microtile from four rows at one column to one row across four 32-column stripes, retaining four independent FP32 accumulators per thread.
Changed the CTA output shape to 8x128 while retaining 256 threads and 1024 outputs per CTA; warp lanes traverse contiguous columns within each stripe.
Added tail guards for rows and each column stripe, with size_t matrix offsets and one alpha/beta application per valid output.
